sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, match the columns or one word).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) Competitors are the business ________ who run the same business and offer similar products in the market. (b) In ________ pricing an organisation keeps a low price to increase sales and market share.
Identify True or False. (a) Sales promotion is impersonal in nature. (b) Advertising does not provide immediate feedback.
questions.answer: (a) False: it is personal in nature. (b) True.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks. (a) ________ is the act of conveying information for creating mutual understanding (communication). (b) ________ in its simplest form can be described as a process of achieving voluntary exchange between customers and producers.

Identify True or False. (a) Tourism marketing is the process of achieving voluntary exchanges between tourists and organisations. (b) Market research is the systematic investigation of the facts relevant to various aspects of marketing.

questions.answer: (a) True. (b) False: selling is a part of marketing.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Explain any two importance of discount pricing.
questions.answer: It increases sales by offering a lower price in a season or on a quantity. It helps clear stock and attracts price-sensitive customers.

or.q: Explain any two principles of effective writing.
or.answer: Unity and coherence make the message one idea and clear. Accuracy and briefness make it correct and saves time.

questions.q: Describe any two characteristics of tourism marketing.
questions.answer: Tourism marketing sells an experience, not a tangible product, so services are inseparable and perishable. There is no transfer of ownership and the service varies because humans are involved.

questions.q: Give two differences between marketing and selling.
questions.answer: Marketing is market-oriented and starts with the buyer's needs; selling is product-oriented and starts with the seller. Marketing is broader and includes selling; in marketing the consumer determines price.

questions.q: What is meant by segmentation? Give an example.
questions.answer: Segmentation is identifying groups of buyers with different needs. For example a tour package designed for religious tourists serves one segment.

questions.q: What is the marketing mix?
questions.answer: It is the set of controllable tools a firm blends to get the response it wants: product, price, promotion and place, with people, physical evidence and process added for services.

questions.q: State any two features of advertising.
questions.answer: It is a paid form of communication. It is impersonal (one-way) and has an identified sponsor.

questions.q: Name any two types of selling techniques.
questions.answer: Direct selling and retail selling (also agency, tele-sales, door-to-door, business-to-business, mail order and online).

questions.q: What is promotional pricing? Give an example.
questions.answer: A temporary price below cost to increase short-term sales. Example: a Delhi–Mumbai return flight for Rs 2,000 if travelled within a week.

questions.q: Who are the intermediaries in the marketing environment?
questions.answer: They are wholesalers, retailers and agents who help bring the product to the consumer and create place and time utility.

questions.q: Explain what CRM is.
questions.answer: Customer Relationship Management is managing a company's interactions with current and future customers to build, maintain and sustain relations and loyalty.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the macro environment of tourism marketing (three factors).
questions.answer: (i) Political environment: laws and policies such as FDI affect business. (ii) Economic and demographic environment: purchasing power, inflation, population size and income. (iii) Technological and socio-cultural environment: internet booking and the values, beliefs and customs of society.

questions.q: Distinguish between advertising and sales promotion (three points).
questions.answer: (i) Advertising is impersonal; sales promotion is personal. (ii) Advertising aims at creating demand; sales promotion aims at increasing sales. (iii) Advertising reaches a huge audience but gives no immediate feedback; sales promotion has limited scope and gives immediate feedback.

questions.q: Explain any three methods of sales promotion in tourism.
questions.answer: (i) Discount coupons let consumers avail discounts on purchase. (ii) Free samples and trade shows or exhibitions create awareness. (iii) Price discounts by airlines, flyer clubs, hotel premiums and incentives to travel agents.

questions.q: Explain any three pricing strategies.
questions.answer: (i) Penetration pricing: a low price to gain market share. (ii) Skimming: a high price lowered slowly for innovative products. (iii) Psychological pricing (Rs 999) and discount pricing (seasonal sale).

questions.q: Explain any three distribution channels in tourism.
questions.answer: (i) Travel agents are retailers who sell to tourists for a commission. (ii) Tour operators and wholesalers buy in volume and make packages. (iii) Online travel companies such as makemytrip and national, state and local tourism agencies.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the functions of marketing with reference to tourism, in six points.
questions.answer: (i) Market research: systematic investigation to know tourists' needs. (ii) Product planning and development: designing and improving products such as tour packages. (iii) Segmentation: grouping tourists by needs, e.g. religious tourists. (iv) Promotion: informing and persuading through advertising, publicity, personal selling and sales promotion. (v) Selling: direct, retail, agency, tele-sales and online. (vi) The marketing mix of the four Ps plus people, physical evidence and process guides these functions.

questions.q: Explain advertising and the media used in the tourism business, in six points.
questions.answer: (i) Advertising is a paid, impersonal, one-way communication by an identified sponsor. (ii) Its purpose is awareness, interest, sales and attitude change (AIDAS). (iii) Press media include newspapers, magazines, brochures and leaflets. (iv) Broadcast media include radio, television, cinema and video. (v) The internet is the latest and most effective medium. (vi) Aerial, railway and off-the-wall media are also used and media are chosen by reach, frequency and cost.

questions.q: Explain Customer Relationship Management and its steps, in six points.
questions.answer: (i) CRM manages interactions with current and future customers. (ii) It aims at customer satisfaction and loyalty. (iii) It collects information and builds a customer database. (iv) It obtains and analyses customer requirements. (v) It develops products as per the requirements and keeps personal communication. (vi) Hotels use guest profiles to personalise service.
